correspondence.component_scope: chosen eastern opening and cross gully transfer
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is within low, ponded tundra beside a small valley. Its northwest-then-west selected continuation traverses several separate south-trending gullies and pond chains with intervening interfluves. A large east-west incised watercourse lies farther south, but that does not itself establish the selected cross-gully transfer. The focused original did not show a continuous receiving floor linking the opening westward into the chosen southwest valley.

correspondence.component_scope: southwest receiving valley and southern bend
correspondence.finding: At the western end of the opening region, the inspected river valley turns southwest through gullied terrain and broadens among small ponds before joining the larger westward river. Upper and middle originals overlap across this junction and the southern bend. Ordinary valley correspondence is supported without imposing the selected line on a particular wet thread.

correspondence.component_scope: middle westward meandering and braided corridor
correspondence.finding: The large westward river has a continuous winding floodplain that gradually broadens into braids; side streams join from the surrounding ponded upland. The selection follows the same west-to-west-northwest receiving corridor. Adjoining lakes remain individually unnamed, and their proximity is not treated as proof the selection crosses them.

correspondence.component_scope: lower braided receiving river and delta
correspondence.finding: The broad braided belt runs west through ponded lowlands and opens into a large coastal delta. Continuous ordinary receiving-floor correspondence is visible through the main channel and southern marginal delta. CHS identifies the large braided river mouth at this receiving bay as Storkerson River, while distinguishing other surrounding coastal rivers and harbour streams.

correspondence.component_scope: source terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The separately stored source endpoint lies on the landward southern marginal delta/alluvial surface near a side-channel/coastal approach. The continuous delta receives the lower river and opens westward into marine water. The point is not asserted to be an exact active river-mouth vertex or open seawater.

correspondence.component_scope: render terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The separately stored rendered ending extends north within the same low marginal delta/ponded surface. Its ordinary terminal receiving setting is established, while its precise present land/water boundary and tidal status remain unassigned. No extra natural river reach or corrected endpoint is invented.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen western opening and ice nunatak passage
correspondence.finding: The chosen western opening and first eastward parts lie in the mapped ice-and-perennial-snow mountain belt among exposed-rock islands west of the Gerard de Geer trunk. The complete opening and successive ice/rock passages are visible on the detailed original. No specific name is assigned to the initial ice passage or its adjacent nunataks, and no mapped natural-river identity is inferred from the model line.

correspondence.component_scope: gerard de geer glacier and northern margin
correspondence.finding: The selected line turns south across the ice corridor directly labeled Gerard de Geer Gletscher, then continues east along its northern rock-and-ice margin and bends southeast near the eastern margin. The original depicts the glacier trough, adjoining bedrock promontories and all intervening selected joins. The generalized line is not treated as a surveyed meltwater channel or proof of a current route through or beneath the ice.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern margin to parallel covered valley
correspondence.finding: The selection passes the glacier-side rock margin and the northern covered-valley junction, then follows the southward valley immediately east of the bedrock ridge bordering the inner Isfjord arm. The map continuously exposes this glacier/rock/covered-valley transition and the receiving valley. The parallel Isfjord water arm lies west of this land interval and is not substituted for the selected valley or used as its river name.

correspondence.component_scope: lower covered valley and lateral joins
correspondence.finding: The lower southeastward selection continues along the same broadly mapped undifferentiated-cover valley, with several lateral covered valleys joining from the east. Its final approach reaches the bay-head setting labeled Renbugten. All lower bends, valley junctions and the coastal approach are visible in the original; no separate selected lake passage or lake-transfer gap is indicated. No natural-river name is printed along this selected valley in the inspected map.

correspondence.component_scope: separate source and render terminal settings
correspondence.finding: Both supplied terminal positions were considered separately against enlarged original pixels. The source endpoint is landward on the western rock flank of the Renbugten bay-head setting; the rendered endpoint extends farther south to the mapped coastal margin beside the bay. These are within the same ordinary Renbugten/Isfjord receiving setting, but neither the inventory's sea class nor the generalized placement establishes a precise ordinary river mouth. Renbugten is a bay label and Isfjord a fjord label, not a river hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected Blanco Creek opening and southeast headward reach
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is within the mapped Blanco Creek drainage beside the Bee–Goliad boundary. Intermittent channel symbols, repeated creek labels and intervening tributary joins follow the selected southeast corridor. The selection begins downstream of the creek’s full natural headwaters; no new source location is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward Blanco Creek turn, Berclair crossing and southward continuation
correspondence.finding: The original shows the same continuous Blanco Creek corridor through the eastward turn, US59/Berclair setting and southward boundary reach. Small pools, road crossings and joining drains remain in this mapped receiving corridor. No separate-basin transfer or missing lake-to-feeder link is indicated.

correspondence.component_scope: Blanco Creek east and southeast toward Blanconia
correspondence.finding: Repeated Blanco Creek labels and the connected channel/floodplain follow the selected bends and tributary joins across all six stored parts. The route continues past the Blanconia setting into the broader downstream creek valley. Nearby side-drainage labels are not substituted for Blanco Creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Blanco Creek and junction with Medio Creek west of Refugio
correspondence.finding: The broad lower Blanco channel connects directly to the mapped Medio Creek junction west of Refugio, after which Mission River labels begin. Part11 spans the junction setting and the beginning of the receiving river. TSHA’s two place entries independently describe these creeks forming Mission River. Medio Creek is the separate joining tributary, not a selected tributary fragment. Butte Lake is a separately labeled adjacent lake and is not a required selected through-lake transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Mission River past Refugio and into the lower alluvial corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected course occupies the mapped Mission River valley past Refugio and the US77 crossing, then the connected meandering river and floodplain. Joining drains and wetlands are visible. McGuill Lake is separately mapped beside the lower river; the generalized selection passes its riverward setting rather than establishing a distinct passage through that lake. No managed lake or glacier transfer is required.

correspondence.component_scope: Fennessey Flat and lower Mission River wetlands toward the Melon Creek joining area
correspondence.finding: The stored generalized segment traverses the continuous mapped lower river/floodplain wetland complex at Fennessey Flat and reaches the adjoining mouthward receiving waters near Melon Creek. The map shows an integrated river, marsh, pool and channel setting around this traverse. Ordinary receiving-corridor correspondence is complete without claiming that the generalized diagonal follows an active channel, exact bank or present wetland flow path. Melon Creek remains a distinct joining creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Mission River mouth wetlands, delta margin and rendered Mission Bay ending
correspondence.finding: The final part remains in the connected mouthward river/marsh complex and approaches Mission Bay. The stored source endpoint is in the mapped mouth wetland/delta setting near Mission Lake and the bay margin, rather than being forced onto a precise active river channel. The separate rendered endpoint extends farther into the open Mission Bay waterbody. Mission Lake is a separately labeled delta-side lake, not an alias of the river or bay. Mission Bay, described by TSHA as an inlet of Copano Bay, is the actual receiving setting; the selected route is not extended across Copano Bay or to the Gulf.

correspondence.component_scope: western opening and eastward dry floor
correspondence.finding: The chosen western opening lies on a dry, low alluvial surface at the foot of rocky relief. The selected eastward route occupies the same broad floor around projecting low outcrops, approaching the receiving corridor on the eastern side of the hills. The original image and a local enlarged reading of the opening account for the initial portion without demanding a continuously incised or currently wet thread.

correspondence.component_scope: short joins and northward upper corridor
correspondence.finding: The short contiguous parts lead northeast and then north through the dry receiving passage along the rocky foothills. The corridor remains visible between neighboring relief and alluvial surfaces and receives short side gullies. At this generalized scale the selected turn is a continuous valley/footslope receiving floor, rather than an unexplained transfer between separate basins.

correspondence.component_scope: northeastward approach and eastern bend
correspondence.finding: The dry valley runs northeast, opens progressively into broader alluvial ground and bends north beside a long ridge on the east. Branching pale surface traces and lateral fans enter the same receiving lowland. The upper and middle views overlap across the bend, accounting for its continuation at ordinary terrain scale.

correspondence.component_scope: northward alluvial plain to northwestward neck
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the broad northward floor between rocky ridges and turns northwest toward a narrowing below a prominent eastern fan. Multiple dry channel traces share the alluvial floor. The passage continues around the fan's western margin into the next wider receiving corridor; no missing interbasin link is required to explain these parts.

correspondence.component_scope: northwestern receiving fan and saline approach
correspondence.finding: Below the neck, the selected route follows a broad northwestward valley floor with branching pale channel and mineral-surface patterns. Fans descend from the eastern and western relief into this continuous receiving corridor. The middle and lower original views overlap over the small intervening parts and show the transition into the widened northern saline depression.

correspondence.component_scope: actual northern salt pan floor ending
correspondence.finding: The last part enters the widened, pale-edged salt-pan/playa floor, turns north across the low surface and ends near its northern pale margin below rocky relief. The actual source and render endpoint locations coincide in the supplied selection and are both covered by the lower original. The surface extends laterally beyond the selected tip; no river mouth, surveyed natural terminus, current overflow path or specific salar hydronym is inferred from the model's endorheic terminal flag.

correspondence.component_scope: dry surface and managed passage scope
correspondence.finding: The imagery accounts for an arid terrain sequence of dry valleys, joining alluvial fans, broader receiving floors and a northern salt-pan surface. No major open lake, glacier or reservoir passage is established within the selection. Roads, tracks and nearby developed grid patterns do not require an inferred managed interbasin transfer to explain the ordinary geographic corridor. Exact banks, contemporary water presence, sediment chemistry and present infrastructure operation are outside the evidence scope.
